get.summary: Introspect the calling API key: user identity, owning app, scope, USDC balance and remaining spend allowance — one call.

schema.title: Response List App Transfers Api V1 Apps Transfers Get

get.description: Get OMNI, NEAR, EVM and Swipelux wallet balances for authenticated user.

post.description: Price a deposit from any chain into the wallet's Base USDC. Send either `amount` in the origin token or `amountTo` in USDC. The quote is recorded; `POST /balance/payin/quote/submit` opens it.

Open the quote that was priced and answer with what funds it: the `executionContract` naming the deposit address, the amount and the token to send. Never re-priced — a quote whose price no longer holds answers `410 quote_expired`. Status and hashes are filled in by the background route sync once the deposit lands.
Get quote for payout to contact. Auto-detects payment channel (IBAN/onchain/internal).
Estimate payout amount and fees without a contact or provider-side activation.
Execute a persisted quote the account authorized with a signature over the `executionContract` that submit returned. Which channel settles it follows from the quote itself.

Activate a payout quote and create pending records. Answers with what the client has to do: a deposit address to fund, a transaction to broadcast, or — when the returned `executionContract` says `requiresExecution` — typed data to sign and hand back at `/balance/payout/quote/execute`, where nothing is placed until then.

post.summary: Read payout capabilities for one recipient
post.description: What a payout to this recipient would be allowed to do: one option per bank rail of the user's that could reach them, each carrying its limits, fees, memo and purpose-code rules, and the blockers that stand in the way. Reads the provider's live channel catalogue where one exists (Due), falling back to our declarations otherwise. Takes either a saved `contactId` or raw `account` requisites; books, quotes and writes nothing.

Quote a move between two accounts the user owns — USDC<->EURC on the Base wallet, or the wallet <-> a the banking provider USD virtual account. Every solver that can serve the route is compared and `allQuotes` ranks them; `executionContract` says how to execute the winner (docs/balance-swap.md).

Spend the signature the account gave over the `executionContract` that submit returned — a signed order the backend relays, or a move that debits a provider-held fiat balance. A quote the client settles itself is refused here: it needs nothing beyond submit.

Activate a swap quote. Returns the route's settlement instructions: the deposit address to fund, or the transaction to broadcast. When the returned `executionContract` says `requiresExecution`, nothing is placed yet — sign it and call `/balance/swap/quote/execute`.

get.description: Check status of any transaction by quote_id.

Return every supported bank rail. Rails the user has activated come from the Bank table (with status / iban_data); rails the user has not activated are returned from the static BANK_INFO registry with status=not_started and iban_data=None. If a rail's provider KYC is APPROVED but no ACTIVE Bank row exists yet, syncs lazily from Swipelux / Align before returning.

post.description: Create or upsert Bank rows for multiple rails in one request. Returns a per-rail result so one pending or failed rail does not abort the batch.
Issue a new virtual or physical card. User must complete KYC first.

put.summary: Create or update the entity under a client-chosen id
put.description:
Write the entity at this id, creating it if the id is free.

A phone that loses the response to ``POST`` cannot tell a request that
never arrived from one that did, and retrying it would create a second
person. Letting the client choose the id makes the retry land on the same
row — and lets a person and their ownership edge go out together, since
the edge can name an id the client already knows.

Drop the ownership claim; the person goes too unless they own something
else or belong to another user's graph. Their documents are unlinked, not

put.description:
Return the KYB subject, creating it as a company when it is missing.

Every other write needs a subject to hang off, so this is the flow's first
call. It is explicit rather than a side effect of the first save: creating
the subject decides, permanently, whether it is a person or a company.

post.summary: Ask the account's owners to approve a transfer
post.description:
File a transfer for an acting seat on the paying account to authorize.

This is the path for a seat that may not move money itself: nothing is sent
until an owner approves by signing the transfer.

post.summary: Record a request approved by signing it
post.description:
The web app sends the transfer from the account's own wallet through the
normal flow, then posts the hash here: that report is both the approving
vote and the execution receipt.

patch.description: Renames a contact and fills in details it is still missing (address, relationship, BIC, bank address). Values already stored are kept as they are, and whatever the payout providers keep about the recipient is updated on their side too. Use this instead of deleting and re-creating a contact to add a field — a re-created contact is a new row, and the provider beneficiary registered for the original stays behind on it.

businessIndustry.title: Businessindustry
businessIndustry.description: 6-digit NAICS 2022 industry code for business recipients. Required by Swipelux before US ACH payout destinations of business recipients can be activated; ignored for individual recipients.

AerodromeRoutePayload.title: AerodromeRoutePayload
AerodromeRoutePayload.description: Persisted form of one Aerodrome path hop.

AerodromeSettlementPayload.title: AerodromeSettlementPayload
AerodromeSettlementPayload.description: Canonical Aerodrome path pinned when the pool is quoted.

AffiliatedToInfo.title: AffiliatedToInfo
AffiliatedToInfo.description:
The affiliate behind this account, as seen from ``GET /user``.

``role`` is the affiliate's team seat on this account, or ``None`` when the
affiliate merely referred it and holds no seat — that distinction is what
separates a partner-managed company from a plain referral. ``full_access``
mirrors the same seat: only an ``owner`` shares ownership of the account.

AlignSettlementPayload.title: AlignSettlementPayload
AlignSettlementPayload.description: Canonical Align destination selected at quote time.

AppMeResponse.title: AppMeResponse
AppMeResponse.description:
Everything an API-key client needs to know about itself in one call.

Returned by ``GET /apps/me``. Avoids the older multi-step dance of
``GET /user`` + ``GET /apps/{id}`` + ``GET /balance`` for callers (e.g.
the CLI) that only have an ``X-Api-Key`` and want to introspect.

BankAddressDetails.title: BankAddressDetails
BankAddressDetails.description:
The beneficiary bank's own address, kept apart from the holder's.

Read/storage shape: only the street is guaranteed, because rows saved before
this was structured hold a single free-text line that validates into
``address_line1`` alone. New input goes through BankAddressInput, which
requires everything the banking provider does.

BankAddressInput.title: BankAddressInput
BankAddressInput.description:
What a client must provide for a bank address: everything the banking provider requires.

the banking provider caps the street at 120 and the city at 80; the country is what the
payout carries in ``bankAddress.country`` (both ISO alpha-2 and alpha-3 are
accepted there), though a payout prefers the BIC-derived one.

BankCapabilities.title: BankCapabilities
BankCapabilities.description: Payout capabilities of a bank rail, derived from static configuration.

BankRail.title: BankRail
BankRail.description: Client-visible bank transfer route; provider identity lives separately.

BankRequestedRailSettings.title: BankRequestedRailSettings
BankRequestedRailSettings.description:
User interest in a bank rail group.

``requested_at`` records when the user last requested this rail, so admin
views can show exactly when each rail was requested — the pooled/named
distinction is intentionally not timestamped separately (rail requests will
drop that split entirely in the future). Absent for opt-ins made before
timestamps were tracked.

BankRequestedRails.title: BankRequestedRails
BankRequestedRails.description: Rails the user is interested in opening.

BankResponse.title: BankResponse
BankResponse.description:
Bank row as returned to clients.

Merges static rail metadata (from BANK_INFO) with per-user state. For rails
the user hasn't activated yet, ``id`` / ``external_account_id`` / ``created_at``
are ``None`` and ``status`` is ``not_started``.

BankTimeToOpen.title: BankTimeToOpen
BankTimeToOpen.description: Expected wait time before a bank rail becomes usable.

accountHolderName.title: Accountholdername
accountHolderName.description: Beneficiary name the contact will carry. Checked against the 22-character NACHA receiver-name limit on ach; ignored on every other rail.

BankValidationRequest.title: BankValidationRequest
BankValidationRequest.description: Request to prevalidate bank details before creating a contact.

BanksListResponse.title: BanksListResponse
BanksListResponse.description: List bank rails plus user's requested rail preferences.

BatchContractInvoiceRequest.title: BatchContractInvoiceRequest
BatchContractInvoiceRequest.description:
Per-contract invoice options for batch invoicing.

A call without ``finalize`` creates the period invoice as a DRAFT (or
updates its items if a DRAFT already exists). Both the client and the
contractor may edit a DRAFT. Setting ``finalize=True`` additionally moves
the invoice to SENT, generates the PDF and emails the client — only the
client (contract owner) is allowed to finalize.

BillingCycle.title: BillingCycle
BillingCycle.description: Calendar cadence a contract bills on.

BillingCycleInput.title: BillingCycleInput
BillingCycleInput.description:
The calendar schedule a contract bills on.

``endsOn`` anchors the cycle: a day of month (``"1".."31"`` or ``"last"``)
for monthly/quarterly/yearly, a weekday name for weekly/biweekly. It is
rejected for a one-time contract.

activated.title: Activated
activated.description: True if card details have been revealed and cached

dailySpend.title: Dailyspend
dailySpend.description: Total spent today on this card (from fiat_transfers)

CardResponse.title: CardResponse
CardResponse.description: Card response - universal format for any provider.

nonce.title: Nonce
nonce.description: Unix timestamp used in the signed message (valid 5 min)

CardRevealRequest.title: CardRevealRequest
CardRevealRequest.description: Request to reveal card details. Requires wallet signature.

CardsPreApproveResponse.title: CardsPreApproveResponse
CardsPreApproveResponse.description: Pre-flight info for issuing the card provider cards.

ChainCatalogResponse.title: ChainCatalogResponse
ChainCatalogResponse.description: The whole catalog, as clients mirror it.

ChainConfigResponse.title: ChainConfigResponse
ChainConfigResponse.description: One chain: canonical identity, per-provider identifiers, tokens.

ClientSignature.title: ClientSignature
ClientSignature.description: Client's answer to a signing request, sent with ``/quote/submit``.

iban.title: Iban
iban.description: Bank account details in the same format as /banks ibanData

ContactLinkedUserResponse.title: ContactLinkedUserResponse
ContactLinkedUserResponse.description: Linked HEVN user preview for contact.

ContactRelationship.title: ContactRelationship
ContactRelationship.description:
How a payout contact relates to the user.

The vocabulary mirrors Swipelux's recipient relationships so the common
values project onto their API unchanged, but this is our own domain type:
``SELF`` marks a first-party payout to the user's own account at another
bank and has no Swipelux counterpart. Providers own that projection — see
``SwipeluxRecipients._recipient_relationship`` — so nothing here depends on
a provider, and no provider enum has to carry a value it cannot accept.

ContactResponse.title: ContactResponse
ContactResponse.description: Contact response with full structure for transfer.

bic.title: Bic
bic.description: BIC for an IBAN contact saved without one — Align requires it on IBAN beneficiaries. Ignored when the contact already has a BIC.

bankAddress.description: The beneficiary bank's own address (street + city), required by the banking provider payouts. Parts the contact already carries are kept; missing ones are filled, so a legacy free-text address can gain its city.

ContactUpdateRequest.title: ContactUpdateRequest
ContactUpdateRequest.description:
Request to update a contact.

The display name is freely mutable. Requisites, address and relationship
are *fill-only*: a field that is already set on the contact keeps its
value, and only the still-empty ones are filled in. Recreating the contact
to add a missing field is what produced duplicate rows — the requisites
identity changes with the added field, so the upsert misses the original
and its provider account ids are stranded on the deleted row.

ContactWalletResponse.title: ContactWalletResponse
ContactWalletResponse.description: Wallet payment method block used by invoice/payment method schemas.

ContractDocument.title: ContractDocument
ContractDocument.description: A document attached to a contract.

ContractLastInvoice.title: ContractLastInvoice
ContractLastInvoice.description: Flat last-invoice data embedded in contract responses.

ContractLineItem-Input.title: ContractLineItem
ContractLineItem-Input.description: One billable line of a contract.

ContractLineItem-Output.title: ContractLineItem
ContractLineItem-Output.description: One billable line of a contract.

ContractParty-Output.title: ContractParty
ContractParty-Output.description: Minimal user data embedded in contract responses.

ContractRateType.title: ContractRateType
ContractRateType.description: How a contractor's fee is computed.

ContractSchedulePeriod.title: ContractSchedulePeriod
ContractSchedulePeriod.description: One billing occurrence, as the client renders it.

ContractScheduleResponse.title: ContractScheduleResponse
ContractScheduleResponse.description: The resolved calendar schedule of a contract.

ContractStatus.title: ContractStatus
ContractStatus.description: Contract status. A contract is live the moment it is created.

ContractTermsInput-Input.title: ContractTermsInput
ContractTermsInput-Input.description: Commercial terms a client sets on a contract.

ContractTermsInput-Output.title: ContractTermsInput
ContractTermsInput-Output.description: Commercial terms a client sets on a contract.

ContractType.title: ContractType
ContractType.description: What the recurring agreement is for. A label only — it drives no logic.

CorporateAuthorityDocumentIds.title: CorporateAuthorityDocumentIds
CorporateAuthorityDocumentIds.description: Canonical authority-document references exposed by the KYB structure.

CowOrder.title: CowOrder
CowOrder.description:
The order the trader signs and the order book stores.

Built verbatim from what ``POST /quote`` returned (plus the receiver) — the
backend never recomputes CoW's fee or price math.

CowOrderKind.title: CowOrderKind
CowOrderKind.description: Which side of the order is fixed.

CowSwapSettlementPayload.title: CowSwapSettlementPayload
CowSwapSettlementPayload.description: Canonical CoW order and relay metadata.

CowTokenBalance.title: CowTokenBalance
CowTokenBalance.description: Where the tokens are sourced from / delivered to.

CreateContractRequest.title: CreateContractRequest
CreateContractRequest.description:
Create a recurring billing agreement.

Exactly one of ``contractorEmail`` or ``clientEmail`` must be set:
``contractorEmail`` means the caller is the client, ``clientEmail`` means
the caller is the contractor.

CreateInvoiceFromContractRequest.title: CreateInvoiceFromContractRequest
CreateInvoiceFromContractRequest.description:
Create a one-off invoice for a contract's current billing period.

Either party may call it; the invoice always flows from the contract's
contractor to its client. Line items default to the contract's terms.

discount.title: Discount
discount.description: Fixed discount in invoice currency. Subtracted from sum of items.

iban.title: Iban
iban.description: Custom bank requisites in the same ibanData format as POST /user/contact. Each entry is snapshotted onto the invoice alongside any `banks`/`onchain` methods, so several payment options can be offered at once.

wallets.title: Wallets
wallets.description: Custom crypto wallet requisites (network + address + currency). Snapshotted onto the invoice alongside `iban`/`banks`/`onchain`.

CreateInvoiceRequest.title: CreateInvoiceRequest
CreateInvoiceRequest.description:
Request to create an invoice.

Participant data (email, display_name, address) is snapshotted at creation time.
Amount is computed as sum of items[].price * items[].quantity.
invoice_number is auto-generated per (contractor, client) pair.

CreateUploadedInvoiceRequest.title: CreateUploadedInvoiceRequest
CreateUploadedInvoiceRequest.description:
Create an incoming invoice from a manually uploaded/local document.

Current user is the client/payer. Payment methods are resolved from saved
contacts; direct paymentMethods input is intentionally not accepted.

Currency.title: Currency
Currency.description: Supported invoice/contract currencies. G10 majors + AED/HKD, plus popular crypto tokens.

DepositToken.title: DepositToken
DepositToken.description:
Stablecoin a virtual account delivers on-chain for a fiat deposit.

USDC everywhere; EURC only where a live account can be re-pointed at it.

signature.description: Signing state for a HEVN-generated document. ``null`` when the document carries no signature blocks, so a plain upload stays plain. A stored document is not a signed one — read the state.

DocumentExportFormat.title: DocumentExportFormat
DocumentExportFormat.description: Output format for the formal account documents (statement / confirmation).

DocumentSignatureInfo.title: DocumentSignatureInfo
DocumentSignatureInfo.description: Typed view of the ``content["hellosign"]`` block for API responses.

DocumentSignatureState.title: DocumentSignatureState
DocumentSignatureState.description:
Where one generated document stands with the signing provider.

A document that exists is not a document that is signed: the UI has to tell
a fresh draft from one waiting on a signer from a completed one.

DocumentType.title: DocumentType
DocumentType.description: Open internal document type; providers map it to their own taxonomy.

Eip712SigningRequest.title: Eip712SigningRequest
Eip712SigningRequest.description:
Typed data the client signs off-chain, plus its pre-computed digest.

``types`` deliberately omits ``EIP712Domain``: ethers v5 rejects it and viem
does not need it. ``digest`` is the full EIP-712 hash — an EOA signs it
directly, the Base smart wallet signs its replay-safe wrapping and returns
the wrapped ERC-1271 bytes.

corporateAuthorityDocumentIds.description: Expose typed authority IDs without creating a second source of truth.

taxId.title: Taxid
taxId.description: As the registry issues it. No shape is imposed — the per-country pattern the provider sends in the requirement constraints is the only one that applies. The bound is a size guard, not a format.

EntityDraftWrite.title: EntityDraftWrite
EntityDraftWrite.description: Create or partially update an entity from the KYB draft editor.

EntityIdentityDocument.title: EntityIdentityDocument
EntityIdentityDocument.description:
Issuing metadata for one identity document held by a person entity.

The scanned pages live in ``Entity.documents`` keyed by upload slot
(``passport_front``, ``id_card_back``, …); this carries what the slot
cannot express and what providers ask for: the document's own type, the
country that issued it and its number.

title.title: Title
title.description: Office held in the target company, for example 'Director'.

EntityRelationshipDraftUpdate.title: EntityRelationshipDraftUpdate
EntityRelationshipDraftUpdate.description: Editable relationship terms; endpoints and consent status stay fixed.

title.title: Title
title.description: Office held in the target company, for example 'Director'.

EntityRelationshipDraftWrite.title: EntityRelationshipDraftWrite
EntityRelationshipDraftWrite.description: Create or partially update a relationship in the KYB graph.

EntityRelationshipStatus.title: EntityRelationshipStatus
EntityRelationshipStatus.description: Consent state for a KYB ownership or authority relationship.

EvmTransactionRequest.title: EvmTransactionRequest
EvmTransactionRequest.description: An EVM transaction the client signs and broadcasts from its wallet.

quoteId.title: Quoteid
quoteId.description: The `quoteId` the quote was issued under — the same one submit was called with, since submit answers with no id of its own — or the SHA-256 of the quote amount, recipient and idempotency key that the signed typed data names. Both address the same quote. Every id we issue is a bare one of ours: no channel prefix and no provider marker, whichever rail priced it.

signature.description: Base smart wallet signature over the payout typed data (`scheme: eip1271`). The backend rebuilds the digest from the stored quote and asks the wallet's isValidSignature about it.

ExecutePayoutQuoteRequest.title: ExecutePayoutQuoteRequest
ExecutePayoutQuoteRequest.description:
Execute a persisted the banking provider fiat payout quote.

Authorized by the smart wallet's ERC-1271 signature over the quote's
`executionContract.typedData`.

ExecuteSwapQuoteRequest.title: ExecuteSwapQuoteRequest
ExecuteSwapQuoteRequest.description:
Execute a swap quote the account authorized with a signature.

Sent when submit's `executionContract` says `requiresExecution`.

ExecutionContract.title: ExecutionContract
ExecutionContract.description:
Everything the client needs to execute one quote.

One format for every channel: crypto routes carry deposit / transaction /
order instructions, the banking provider fiat payouts carry the typed data to sign and the
arguments that reproduce the quote hash. ``canonical_payload`` pins what was
quoted — the provider payload persisted with a crypto route (``/submit``
relays from it, never from client input), or the canonical JSON a the banking provider
quote id is hashed from.

FiatPaymentType.title: FiatPaymentType

IBANStatus.title: IBANStatus
IBANStatus.description:
IBAN account status.

State machine:
``not_started`` → ``requested`` → ``document_requested`` → ``approved`` → ``pending`` → ``active``

- ``not_started``       — default for every rail until the user opts in.
- ``requested``         — user asked for this rail via /pre-approve; awaiting KYC.
- ``document_requested``— admin asked the user for more documents (KYB).
- ``approved``          — KYB passed, account ready to be created at provider.
- ``pending_kyc``       — provider rejected creation until KYC is approved.
- ``pending``           — provider accepted/created the account, waiting.
- ``active``            — real bank details are attached to the row.
- ``frozen`` / ``closed``— terminal/blocked states.

UniversalQuoteResponse.title: UniversalQuoteResponse
UniversalQuoteResponse.description:
What a quote prices, and nothing else.

Rail rules — whether a reference is accepted, the floor on the amount, the
fee schedule behind it — belong to
``POST /balance/payout/recipient/capabilities``, which the client reads
before it prices anything. Repeating them here only gave two sources for
one fact.

What this price *is*, on the other hand, includes how far it can move:
``minToAmount`` and ``slippageBps`` are not rail rules but this quote's own
worst case, and only the provider that priced it knows them.

- `paidAt` optionally backdates the payment; defaults to now.
